newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand voters advised to take their brollies.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand voters advised to take their brollies.

text.p: Sunshine will be at a premium and most people can expect damp, humid, windy but mild conditions for Saturday's election, MetService's chief meteorologist August Auer said on Thursday.
"You'll probably want to go to the polls with a brolly under your arm," he told Reuters.
There was no weather system that should keep people from voting but inclement weather may deter some voters, particularly the elderly, he said.

"Some people who find the rain a bit irritating... they may be inclined to stay home, but we're not looking for any episodic weather that would prevent people getting to the polls had they wanted to."

"It just looks like a moist north-westerly flow over the country so most places with western, coastal exposures will probably first of all be cloudy and have gusty north-westerlies peppered with rain showers," he said.
Northland, Auckland and Taranaki would be particularly subject to such weather paterns.
The centre of the North Island would have less rain but annoying wind, while the east coast of both islands would have the best weather -- still with blustery wind, even gale force in Hawkes Bay.

"It will only be eastern districts that will have bright sun-shiny conditions. The rest of the country will have certainly cloudy skies, the wind will be a bit of an annoyance but none of this, from a weatherman's point of view, should be sufficient to keep people away from the polls."
